title: Stable Personal Signal placement with rendezvous hashing and explicit star pins

scope.subject: Personal content-to-YEIS-star placement stability under catalog/order changes

research_summary: Replace modulo-N auto placement, which remaps most content whenever the eligible marker count changes, with identity-based rendezvous/HRW ranking. Add explicit star pin metadata and a stable placement key so important content can retain a permanent astronomical address while ordinary content remains automatic and stateless.

sources.finding: RFC 2992 contrasts modulo-N with Highest Random Weight and notes modulo-N is highly disruptive when the destination set changes, while HRW provides minimal disruption.
The MIT hrw-hash package demonstrates a compact dependency-free JavaScript HRW implementation whose ranking is independent of destination order and minimally affected by destination-set changes.
Jump Consistent Hash provides fast minimal-memory remapping, but its bucket model assumes sequentially numbered buckets, which is a weaker fit for identity-addressed stars.
Astro Content Collections remain the canonical typed content source; the missing capability is deterministic spatial placement, not another CMS or content runtime.

search_ladder.conclusion: The repository already has its selected content product and universe engine; this task only changes deterministic assignment semantics between those existing layers.
No new framework is required for a stateless key-to-star assignment primitive inside the existing Astro and YEIS architecture.
Astro Content Collections already own typed content ingestion, so placement should remain a narrow subsystem beneath that existing source rather than introduce another content platform.
HRW/rendezvous hashing directly addresses minimal-remapping identity-based assignment; Jump Hash and an npm HRW package were also evaluated as narrower implementation choices.

candidates.name: Identity-based Rendezvous / HRW placement
candidates.source: RFC 2992 algorithm semantics with a narrow project-local deterministic score primitive
candidates.reason: Directly fixes modulo remapping, is independent of marker ordering, works with stable YEIS star identities, requires no lookup table, and avoids adding a runtime dependency for a tiny project-specific adapter.

candidates.name: hrw-hash npm package
candidates.reason: It solves the same primitive cleanly, but adding a package and public API surface is unnecessary when the product needs only a narrow deterministic score/rank adapter already expressed by the standard algorithm.

candidates.name: Jump Consistent Hash
candidates.reason: It is excellent for dense sequential buckets but Personal Universe destinations are stable star identities that can appear/disappear independently; HRW fits identity-addressed arbitrary sets without assigning bucket ordinals.

decision.rationale: Reuse the mature HRW/rendezvous assignment semantics while keeping the implementation as a narrow project adapter over stable content keys and YEIS star identities. Add explicit pin metadata for curated landmarks, preserving the sparse-real-content architecture without a new runtime dependency.
decision.fallback: If content scale later makes O(entries×eligible-stars) ranking material, retain the same placement contract and replace only the ranking backend with a proven indexed/weighted HRW implementation.
